steps.title: Prepare the bridge before scanning
steps.body: In Connect, click the main Connect phone button once. Wait for Phone setup ready and for Desktop bridge and Phone backend to report Running and Ready. Scannable QR codes appear only after that. Read the connection message on failure; rescanning cannot fix a backend that never became ready.

steps.title: Pair from the phone app
steps.body: Choose Android or iPhone under Pair your phone, open the phone app, and scan the QR from inside the app. Tap Connect on the phone. Confirm Connected on the phone, then send 'Hello from my phone' and wait for a text reply. Keep the QR private; if scanning fails, use Manual pairing for displayed setup details.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Verify the exchange, not the indicator
steps.body: A green service light means the desktop services are prepared; it does not prove a phone is connected. The real success check is the assistant text reply in the phone app. If the phone shows Connected but no reply arrives, confirm the same local network before retrying.

steps.title: Add the optional Internet relay
steps.body: After a working LAN exchange, open Internet. Follow the displayed instructions to sign in to the NC Relay account on both desktop and phone. The encrypted peer path still relies on the desktop being running. Record the phone’s live connection state and Active peer connections, then send another short text.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Recognize a working relay test
steps.body: A signed-in account alone is not the test. Successful relay traffic requires a live peer shown in Active peer connections and a text reply arriving on the phone away from the LAN. If no peer appears, check relay readiness and matching accounts. You can keep using LAN in the meantime.

steps.title: Test speech before raising quality
steps.body: In Media, note the current Quality preset and leave it unchanged for the first playback test. Request one short voice reply and confirm you hear it in the phone app. If it stutters, change one quality setting and reconnect the phone. Keep settings modest to avoid unnecessary data.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Know which quality control you changed
steps.body: The Quality preset bundles Opus (kbit/s), H.264 target (kbit/s), Video maximum width (px) and Video frames per second. Editing a bundle value directly changes only that field; the preset label may not follow. Cache idle animations on phone is optional and needs a compatible native build.

steps.title: Read traffic after one short exchange
steps.body: Open Data usage after a text exchange. Counters combine traffic from all phones over LAN and Internet, with media and application totals plus estimated transport overhead. Overhead is extra connection traffic beyond content. These are estimates, not a mobile operator bill. Note totals, play a short reply, then compare again.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Reset without expecting a disconnect
steps.body: Reset statistics clears counters but leaves connections active. Use it when you want a fresh measurement for a single playback test. If numbers grow but nothing plays, inspect phone playback and Advanced service health before resetting again. A nonzero counter alone does not prove a successful reply.

steps.title: Fix one component at a time
steps.body: In Advanced, expand Individual controls and read Service status for Desktop bridge and Phone backend. Identify the stopped or failed component before using its start or stop action. Keep the error visible while you read it, and fix that reported problem rather than restarting every NC provider.
steps.target_hint: This control may depend on available content or a loaded addon. Read the step here; no service or provider is enabled by the guide.

steps.title: Distinguish main Stop from NC power
steps.body: The main Stop button disconnects Internet and stops both remote services while keeping your account signed in. It is separate from Main Chat’s runtime power button. After a deliberate restart, wait for services to become ready and confirm Connected on the phone again before resuming tests.
